note: The roads the car takes when the network doesn't carry people (src/sim/traffic.ts, docs/design/gridlock.md §2): each stretch is a Department for Transport count point, with its 2024 average annual daily flow (all motor vehicles, both ways) as the DfT published it, `estimated` where the DfT estimated it from an earlier count rather than counted it that year. Capacity is the peak hour (`peakShare` of the day's flow) over 0.95: with today's public transport the real road runs at about 0.95 of capacity at the morning peak. `start` is the stretch's load at 08:00 with no public transport at all (the gridlock opening); the traffic the network never touches (`through`: round Manchester, deliveries, the school run) is set from it at load. `serves`: the pairs of places whose drive uses the stretch, as lists of station ids or `corridor:<id>` for every station on a corridor, both ways, with the `share` of those drives that go this way (1 if not given). Lanes each way, free speeds and the shares are from memory of the roads, not survey. Fetched from the DfT's road traffic API (roadtraffic.dft.gov.uk/api/average-annual-daily-flow) on 14 October 2026.
sources: DfT road traffic statistics, average annual daily flow by count point, 2024 (roadtraffic.dft.gov.uk), Stockport and Manchester, fetched 14 October 2026

DfT raw counts at count point 56582 (A57 Hyde Road, manual count, 2024): 1,498 vehicles from 07:00 and 1,744 from 17:00 against a day's 20,629, so the busiest hours are 7 to 8.5% of the day; `peakShare` takes 9%, the usual rule of thumb for urban roads, and `profile` is that count's shape, the night estimated

Census 2011 QS701EW (nomisweb.co.uk): Stockport, 129,896 who travelled, 69.0% drove, 8.6% bus, 5.4% train

TfGM Travel Diary Survey (TRADS) 2022, all trips in Greater Manchester, as reproduced in a Stockport Council paper (democracy.stockport.gov.uk): 40% as car drivers, 17% car passengers; Stockport 45% as drivers
